problems.statement: Central IT is generally unresponsive to Arts (client framing): Arts tickets across the board are slow because ITS does not prioritise Arts.

Routing rule RR-17 sends all SlotBook tickets to an unsupported best-effort P4 queue (0.4 FTE, no target, median 21 days with 17 days before first action); this is the main driver of the Arts resolution gap (about 70% of it).

The policy change was never effectively communicated to Arts: no external notification in the change record, no emails, the ACK-P4 template is silent on best-effort status, and the current manager had no handover. The 2025-08-12 meeting is unverifiable.

ITS Director's claim that Arts was told in person on 2025-08-12 is unproven. The meeting occurred, but the content is unrecorded and the predecessor declined to be interviewed. Even if told, the policy was only communicated verbally to one person and not to the users affected.

Lindqvist satellite campus on-site technician coverage (Tue/Thu only) causes slow on-site hardware resolution, a second and independent contributor that is not Arts-specific (Education has the same delay).

Arts non-SlotBook, remotely handled tickets are handled on par with the rest of the university, and the 2.7x ticket volume is largely SlotBook-driven; Arts non-SlotBook volume is 1.6x average, partly explained by on-site hardware share.
ITS claim that Arts raises trivial and duplicate tickets is not supported: duplicate rate and how-to share are about the same as the rest of the university.
The Philosophy anecdote of general IT failure is a measurement and perception artifact: most of the 3-week delay was waiting on the requester, with under 1 day of active ITS time.
SlotBook tickets are inflated, and possibly worsened, by the 2025-09 SSO migration causing login problems; a flaky-login cause is unverified and SlotBook reportedly was not integrated with SSO.

SlotBook is an unsupported legacy application (PHP 5.6, no documentation, no support agreement, builder departed) creating operational and security risk, and no fit assessment of CampusBook or migration plan exists. CampusBook may not cover multi-section repeating patterns, so ITS's claim of full coverage is unverified.
Service desk capacity constraint (21 FTE, 94% utilisation, down from 23) is a contributing background pressure that makes ITS inclined to ration support, but P2/P3 mostly meet targets.
Arts dissatisfaction (61% vs 24%) is real but survey is low-response and self-selected; it mostly reflects SlotBook and silent non-communication.

causalClaims.from: RR-17 routing of SlotBook tickets to P4 best-effort
causalClaims.to: Slow SlotBook ticket resolution (median 21 days) and most of the Arts resolution gap

causalClaims.from: Absence of notification to affected Arts users and silent ACK-P4 template
causalClaims.to: Arts staff and Dean unaware of best-effort status, perceived unresponsiveness and distrust
Slow on-site hardware resolution for Arts and Education

causalClaims.from: Arts staff raising excessive trivial or duplicate tickets

causalClaims.to: Arts high ticket volume per head

causalClaims.from: Service desk FTE reduction and high utilisation
causalClaims.to: Decision to route SlotBook to best-effort

actions.action: Have ITS and Arts jointly agree an explicit, written service arrangement for SlotBook (interim support level or target, owner, escalation path) and notify Arts formally, including the Dean.
actions.rationale: Addresses the established mechanism (silent P4 routing) cheaply and reversibly without needing to settle who was told in 2025.

actions.action: Change ACK-P4 and the ticket portal to state best-effort status and expected timeframe, and require external notification for routing-rule changes affecting a faculty.
actions.rationale: Removes the silence that turned a policy into perceived unresponsiveness; low cost and reversible.

actions.action: Increase Lindqvist on-site technician coverage, or add remote or locker-based hardware options, affecting Arts and Education.
actions.rationale: Established, Arts-independent contributor with a clear mechanism (4.7 vs 0.6 days to arrival).

actions.action: Commission a requirements-fit assessment of SlotBook vs CampusBook (repeating multi-section patterns) and a costed migration or remediation plan including security risk of PHP 5.6 server.
actions.rationale: No assessment exists; the January 2027 migration claim and the Arts objection are both untested, and this is the root fix.

actions.action: Transfer 2 FTE from the central service desk to create an Arts-run IT desk from spring 2027.
actions.rationale: Does not address the SlotBook support gap or the Lindqvist coverage problem, fragments a desk already at 94% utilisation, and rests on a rejected general-unresponsiveness premise.

actions.action: Place all Arts tickets on the best-effort track, as the ITS Director suggests.
actions.rationale: Non-SlotBook Arts tickets perform on par with others, so this would penalise the wrong set of tickets and make an extreme version of the same silent-policy failure.

actions.action: Force a January 2027 migration to CampusBook without fit validation.
actions.rationale: Six departments timetable about 1,900 sections per term and CampusBook reportedly cannot do repeating multi-section patterns; risk of a term-start scheduling failure.

actions.action: Investigate SlotBook login problems against the SSO change, with access to the server logs.
actions.rationale: Cheap and may reveal an easily fixable cause of ticket volume, but is a minor and unconfirmed contributor.

actions.action: Blame or discipline the former Arts manager or the ITS Director over the 2025-08-12 meeting.
actions.rationale: Content of the meeting is unknowable and the failure is a process gap, not necessarily individual misconduct.

nextEvidence: CampusBook fit assessment against SlotBook's repeating multi-section timetabling patterns, with cost and effort to migrate or to bring SlotBook under support
SlotBook server access logs and login failure data around 2025-09-08 to see whether SSO change drove the Sept-Oct ticket spike and flaky logins

Ticket volume and impact data: counts of tickets after SlotBook was routed to P4 compared with its pre-RR-17 true volume, and any room-clash incident consequences to scope the interim support level needed
output.summary: The Dean's claim of general ITS unresponsiveness is not supported. About 70% of the Arts resolution gap comes from SlotBook tickets, which RR-17 routed to an unsupported 0.4 FTE best-effort queue. Arts was never effectively told: there was no notification, the acknowledgement email was silent, and the 2025-08-12 verbal briefing is unverifiable. A second, non-Arts-specific cause is Lindqvist's Tuesday/Thursday-only on-site coverage. Remotely handled non-SlotBook Arts tickets match the rest of the university, and ITS's trivial-ticket claim is not supported. Fix the SlotBook support arrangement, notification and Lindqvist coverage, and assess CampusBook fit. Avoid the 2 FTE transfer, an all-Arts best-effort track, and a forced January migration.
